question: What types of mechanical resonators have been used to couple with superconducting qubits?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer identifies mechanical resonator types coupled to superconducting qubits, centered on the one-dimensional (on-chip) nanomechanical phononic crystal resonator (lithium niobate), and acknowledges other demonstrated types such as bulk acoustic wave and surface acoustic wave resonators.
examples: a nanomechanical phononic crystal cavity was coupled to a superconducting qubit
one-dimensional phononic crystal resonator coupled to a fluxonium qubit
other demonstrations include bulk acoustic wave and surface acoustic wave resonators

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer states that coupling is realized via the piezoelectric property of lithium niobate and capacitively across a vacuum gap, with the qubit and mechanics fabricated on separate heterogeneously integrated chips; the electromechanical interaction is parametrized by a vacuum Rabi coupling geg between the qubit transition and a single phonon.
examples: piezoelectric coupling in lithium niobate, parametrized by vacuum Rabi coupling geg
qubit and mechanics fabricated on separate chips coupled capacitively across a vacuum gap

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer specifies that the qubit partner is a light fluxonium qubit capacitively coupled to an on-chip readout resonator, preserving charge-noise insensitivity and GHz-frequency readout similar to transmons.
examples: a light fluxonium qubit operating in the light-fluxonium regime
fluxonium circuit capacitively coupled to an on-chip readout resonator with GHz-frequency readout

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer gives the mechanical operating frequency, e.g., ωm/2π ≈ 690 MHz (below 700 MHz), and notes extensibility from 100 to 700 MHz by modifying fluxonium and phononic crystal parameters, with fabrication challenges such as low-EJ junctions (EJ/h < 2 GHz) and deep etching (>250 nm) into lithium niobate.
examples: frequencies below 700 MHz, extendable down to 100 MHz by modifying fluxonium and phononic crystal parameters

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: The answer quantifies the coupling: qubit-phonon coupling rate g/2π ≈ 13.5 MHz (within an order of magnitude of the ultrastrong regime), detuning/swap/geg > 10, and dispersive cooperativities of a few hundred while operating in the QND regime.
examples: coupling rate g/2π ≈ 13.5 MHz, within an order of magnitude of the ultrastrong regime
large dispersive cooperativities of a few hundred with detuning swap/geg > 10

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer notes that the coupling operates in the strong dispersive regime, enabling resolution of individual phonon levels and phonon-number-resolved (QND) measurements of the mechanical population by probing the qubit.
examples: strong dispersive coupling allowing resolution of individual phonon levels
QND measurements of phonon population by probing the qubit excitation spectrum

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer notes that the low operating frequency implies ℏωm/kB T ~ 1 at ~30 mK, so thermal excitations are significant and the mechanical excitation spectrum follows a thermal distribution.
examples: at Teff ~ 30 mK, ℏωm/kBT ~ 1, thermal excitations are common
equilibrium thermal state contains excitations above the ground state

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer mentions enabled applications such as quantum sensing, quantum information processing with phonons, studies of mechanical dissipation and dephasing, and measuring mechanical coherence via flux modulation of the qubit.
examples: new quantum sensing and information processing schemes with phonons
mechanical coherence measured by flux modulating the qubit
dissipation and dephasing study of the mechanical system
